title: Sort Even and Odd Indices Independently
summary: Given an integer array nums, rearrange its elements by sorting the values at odd indices in non-increasing order and the values at even indices in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given an integer array nums, rearrange its elements by sorting the values at odd indices in non-increasing order and the values at even indices in non-decreasing order. For example, if nums = [4,1,2,3], after sorting, it becomes [2,3,4,1]. Return the modified array.
constraints: Sort values originally at even indices in nondecreasing order.
Sort values originally at odd indices in nonincreasing order.
Place the sorted values back only into indices of the same parity.
reference_solution:
def sort_even_odd_indices(nums):
    answer=list(nums)
    answer[::2]=sorted(nums[::2])
    answer[1::2]=sorted(nums[1::2],reverse=True)
    return answer
known_wrong_solutions:

def sort_even_odd_indices(nums):
    answer=list(nums)
    answer[::2]=sorted(nums[::2],reverse=True)
    answer[1::2]=sorted(nums[1::2],reverse=True)
    return answer
hints: Even and odd positions form two independent sequences.
Extract, sort, and assign each parity slice separately.
Sort nums[::2] ascending and nums[1::2] descending, then write both into a copy.
Slice assignment preserves the index parity and the requested sort order within each independent group.
editorial: Slice assignment preserves the index parity and the requested sort order within each independent group.

tests.explanation: Even-index values 4,2 become 2,4; odd-index values 1,3 become 3,1, producing [2,3,4,1].
Each parity group contains one value, so the list stays [2,1].
